name: Resolution Foundation — No half measures: Setting child poverty on a downward course at the Autumn Budget (30 October 2025)

pages_extracted.tool: pdftotext -layout (poppler 26.09.0), one PDF page at a time
pages_extracted.printed_page_rule: printed page = PDF page in both files

citation: Clegg, A. and Judge, L. (2025), No half measures: Setting child poverty on a downward course at the Autumn Budget, Resolution Foundation Spotlight, 30 October 2025.
pdf_metadata: No-half-measures_v2.pdf: 9 pages, CreationDate 2025-10-30 (pdfinfo), 126,154 bytes; Living-Standards-Outlook-2024.pdf: 38 pages, CreationDate 2024-08-29, 835,360 bytes; both HTTP 200 from resolutionfoundation.org on 2026-10-23

model.name: RF projections including use of the IPPR Tax Benefit Model (source_model landman_ttm, the harvest's id for the IPPR model)
model.method: Projections from the latest FRS/HBAI outturn with the IPPR Tax Benefit Model: earnings growth from the OBR's March 2025 EFO; inflation from the Bank of England's August 2025 CPI forecast with an AHC deflator that removes housing costs from CPI; private rents rising with average earnings after a 12-month lag (footnote 4). The cited LSO 2024 Annex: the population is reweighted to ONS projections, including the numbers of dependent children of each age; take-up of Universal Credit is held at 80 per cent and does not change between years or scenarios; modelled changes in incomes and poverty are applied to the outturn year rather than using projected levels. Modelled policy changes occur in April 2026; the Scottish Government's mitigation of the limit is excluded (figure notes).
model.method_basis: raw/pages_layout.txt: No-half-measures_v2.pdf pages 1-3 (figures), 3-4 (Figure 2 notes), 8 (footnote 4), 9 (endnote 8); Living-Standards-Outlook-2024.pdf pages 34 (reweighting), 36 (take-up), 37 (projecting changes rather than levels)

concepts.poverty_line: Relative child poverty after housing costs (60% of median, HBAI definitions per the 'RF analysis of DWP, Households Below Average Income' source line). Neither the spotlight nor the LSO 2024 Annex states whether a policy scenario's line is re-derived from that scenario's median or held at the counterfactual's.
concepts.population: Children; the cited annex reweights 'the numbers of dependent children of each age', the HBAI dependent-child concept.
concepts.period: Financial years; 2029-30 (period 2030) for the reform scores, 'today' = 2025-26 (period 2026).
concepts.counterfactual: RF's current-policy projection at 30 October 2025: pre-Budget policy including the free school meals extension and the UC standard-allowance over-indexation, with the limit in place and Scotland's mitigation excluded.
concepts.cost: £3.5 billion in 2029-30, nominal (unstated whether static; take-up does not change between scenarios per the annex).

reform: Scrap the two-child limit in full from April 2026; endnote 8's partial repeals (three-child limit; two-thirds child element for third and later children; limit lifted for families in work) for 2029-30.
baseline_key: rf_current_policy_projection_2025_10_30 (the harvest's baseline_policy for these claims)
coverage_note: Seven two-child limit figures; each is already a claim of the Autumn Budget 2025 harvest (uk_rf_ab2025, registry uk_ab2025), and the ingest attaches this lane's counterparts to those claims rather than minting duplicates. The spotlight's other figures (baseline rates and counts, FSM, the benefit-cap and LHA package, Figure 3 and Figure 5) stay with the harvest.
diagnosis_upstream: RF's projections and the IPPR model are closed; a divergence classified as an external-model issue becomes a comparison memo.
